precepts.text: Moses had it mapped out: if the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, then ye shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession.
precepts.point: Then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
Before Obadiah's prophecy, the history of the land: when we entered the land, Moses already had it mapped out for us. “If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, every man armed to battle, before the Lord, and the land shall be subdued before you; then ye shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession.”

So you notice: Gad and Reuben, that was to be their land. Gilead was Gad's by the word of Moses. That is why Jeremiah asks, “why then doth their king inherit Gad”: the land was Israel's possession, given before the Lord, and Ammon had no right to it.

precepts.text: And the children of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead, and took it. So Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh held that land. Map shown in class: Ammon sat right next to Gad, and when Gad was carried off, Ammon moved in; and on the modern map that whole area, spelled Amman, is what America calls Jordan today, in Arab hands, exactly as the history in Maccabees explains.
precepts.point: Then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“And the children of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead, and took it, and dispossessed the Amorite which was in it.” So you had Gad, Reuben and Manasseh in that land. But in the prophecy of Obadiah, God says Benjamin shall possess Gilead.

On the ancient map you can see Manasseh, Gad under them, and Reuben under Gad, and right next to Gad was Ammon. When Gad was moved out of the land by the Assyrian captivity, Ammon moved right in. That is what Jeremiah 49:1 says: “their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities.”

After Nebuchadnezzar began to move them out, then the Persians, then the Greeks, the Arabs got the land of Ammon; the Greeks made a deal with them, as the book of the Maccabees tells. On the modern map it is spelled Amman, and that whole area is what America calls Jordan today. It is all Arab land, but it was Ammon and Moab's land, and before that it was Gilead, Israel's land.

precepts.text: None of the men that came up out of Egypt from twenty years old and upward shall see the land, because they have not wholly followed me, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, for they have wholly followed the Lord. The others had doubt in them somewhere; these two had complete faith and never questioned what the Lord told Moses.
precepts.point: And the bones of Joseph, brought up out of Egypt, were buried in Shechem in the parcel of ground Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor.

precepts.text: Be sure your sin will find you out; nothing done in the dark stays hid before the Most High.
precepts.point: The woman had to answer Amen, amen. If you would not agree to drink the water, you showed yourself guilty already, and the guilty were stoned. Surely your sin shall find you out; there is nothing you can hide.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
The priest charged the woman by an oath: if no man had lain with her, “be thou free from this bitter water that causeth the curse”; but if she had gone aside to another instead of her husband, “The Lord make thee a curse and an oath among thy people, when the Lord doth make thy thigh to rot, and thy belly to swell.” The Most High is hard on his daughters for a reason, and he was not playing with that judgment.

The woman had to answer “Amen, amen.” If she would not agree to drink the water, she showed herself guilty already, and the guilty were stoned. “But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.”

There is nothing you can hide. Nothing done in the dark stays hid before the Most High; the bitter water would find out what no man saw.

precepts.text: The men that went up brought an evil report of the land and discouraged the people; that is the history Moses set before Reuben and Gad.
precepts.point: Wherefore discourage ye the heart of the children of Israel from going over into the land which the Lord hath given them: thus did your fathers when they were sent from Kadesh-barnea to see the land. That goes back into the history of the spies in Numbers 13; the fathers were not even in the land yet and were already getting comfortable.

note.label: Numbers 32: The Inheritance of Reuben and Gad on This Side Jordan

precepts.why:
Moses asked Gad and Reuben, “Shall your brethren go to war, and shall ye sit here?” and “wherefore discourage ye the heart of the children of Israel from going over into the land which the Lord hath given them? Thus did your fathers, when I sent them from Kadesh–barnea to see the land.” That goes back into the history of the spies.

“But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we. And they brought up an evil report of the land which they had searched unto the children of Israel, saying, The land, through which we have gone to search it, is a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it are men of a great stature. And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”

The fathers were not even in the land yet and were already getting comfortable; their evil report discouraged the heart of the children of Israel. That is the history Moses set before Reuben and Gad when they asked to sit on this side Jordan while their brethren went to war.

precepts.text: The deal Moses made: go armed before the Lord to war until the land be subdued, and afterward ye shall return and be guiltless, and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.
precepts.point: The word to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh goes back to Numbers 32. They had very much cattle, and when they saw the land on this side Jordan was a good place for it, they asked to dwell there. Moses charged them: before you settle, your armed men pass over before your brethren, all the mighty men of valour, and help them fight; when your brethren have rest and possession, then return to the land of your possession toward the sunrising and enjoy it.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
The word to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh goes back to Numbers 32. They had very much cattle, and when they saw the land on this side Jordan was a good place for it, they asked to dwell there. This was the deal Moses made: “If ye will do this thing, if ye will go armed before the Lord to war, And will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord, until he hath driven out his enemies from before him, And the land be subdued before the Lord: then afterward ye shall return, and be guiltless before the Lord, and before Israel; and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.”

Before you settle, your armed men pass over before your brethren, all the mighty men of valour, and help them fight until the land be subdued; then afterward ye shall return and be guiltless, and this land shall be your possession. That is why Joshua tells them, “Remember the word which Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you”: their wives, little ones and cattle remain, but they pass before their brethren armed until their brethren have rest and possession, and then return to their own land toward the sunrising and enjoy it.

precepts.text: If ye will not do so, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.
precepts.point: The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.” Achan's sin found him out, and Joshua stood in front of him saying, “tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me.”

When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy. Your sin will find you out; the correction is the mercy that comes before the evil.

precepts.text: Moses said if ye will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord until his enemies be driven out, then afterward ye shall return and be guiltless, and this land shall be your possession.
precepts.point: The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

precepts.why:
Joshua tells the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh, “Ye have not left your brethren these many days unto this day, but have kept the charge of the commandment of the Lord your God.” The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: “If ye will do this thing, if ye will go armed before the Lord to war, And will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord, until he hath driven out his enemies from before him, And the land be subdued before the Lord: then afterward ye shall return, and be guiltless before the Lord, and before Israel; and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.”

Whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land. They did it, all of them armed over Jordan until the land was subdued, and so they are guiltless and the land beyond Jordan is theirs.

precepts.text: But if ye will not do so, ye have sinned against the Lord, and be sure your sin will find you out.
precepts.point: The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

precepts.why:
The condition had a warning on the other side of it: “But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.” Had the two and a half tribes stayed home while their brethren fought, that sin would have found them out.

They did not. Joshua's words, “Ye have kept all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you”, are the proof that they kept the charge and did not sin against the Lord in it.

precepts.text: Be sure your sin will find you out; that is exactly what happened to Abimelech.
precepts.point: He reigned only three years. Killing his seventy brothers bought him a three year reign and a crushed skull; it was to no profit. If you are doing wickedness behind closed doors and think the Most High does not see it, he sees it, and he brings swift judgment.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

precepts.why:
“But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.”

That is exactly what happened to Abimelech. He reigned three years and it looked as if the blood of his brothers was behind him, and then a certain woman cast a millstone on his head. If you are doing wickedness behind closed doors and think the Most High does not see it, he sees it, and he brings swift judgment. Be sure your sin will find you out.
